facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is adequate for a credit snapshot, with the limits stated here. On the printed statements, consolidated debt was 68,850 US$m at September 30, 2026 against 68,333 US$m at December 31, 2025, cash was 926 US$m, and Adjusted EBITDA (issuer non-GAAP, consolidated) for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 19,216 US$m, built as FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025. Total debt over that EBITDA is 3.58 times, against 4.28 times for FY2025 and 4.12 times on the March 31, 2026 LTM. The improvement is driven by earnings: Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 is 15,034 US$m against 11,802 US$m, while debt rose. The issuer's own covenant leverage ratio, calculated under a definition not supplied, was 2.83 times at September 30, 2026 and 3.21 times at December 31, 2025, so the covenant basis is lower than the simple ratio at both dates (by 1.07 turns at year-end and 0.75 turns at September 30, 2026, C9). Interest cover on Adjusted EBITDA over cash interest paid is 5.43 times LTM, with cash interest approximated from nine-month figures printed in billions.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Three features limit how far the headline can be read. First, the perimeter mixes the parent's debt (notes and debentures, the Five-Year Credit Facility) with that of Sunoco LP (13,131 US$m of senior notes, bonds and lease-related obligations plus a 111 US$m facility) and USAC (2,350 US$m of senior notes plus a 684 US$m facility), each with separate facilities and creditors; Adjusted EBITDA is consolidated at 100 percent, with 15,209 US$m of noncontrolling interests outside partners' capital. Second, earnings quality: the nine-month 2026 reconciliation adds back 519 US$m of unrealized commodity losses and removes 445 US$m of inventory valuation gains, and Q3 revenue was 37,103 US$m against 19,954 US$m, concentrated in fuel sales of the Sunoco LP segment, so margins are not comparable year on year. Third, claims outside debt (operating leases of 1,862 US$m, preferred units of 2,480 US$m, redeemable noncontrolling interests of 266 US$m, contingent accruals of 536 US$m) and the pending Vaquero acquisition (1.95 billion US$ cash plus about 33.3 million common units) are outside the leverage figures.

facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: Issuer-reported covenant leverage under the Five-Year Credit Facility: 3.21 to 1.00 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:330), 3.16 times for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:14), 3.01 times at June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:17) and 2.83 times at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:18). The facility "limits us, on a rolling four quarter basis, to a maximum Consolidated Funded Indebtedness to Consolidated EBITDA ratio, as defined in the underlying credit agreement, of 5.00 to 1.00, which can generally be increased to 5.50 to 1.00 during a Specified Acquisition Period" (10-K page:330). The headroom against the 5.00 to 1.00 limit is therefore 2.17 turns on the reported 2.83 times (calculated, C9), before any Specified Acquisition Period increase. The covenant definition differs from this handoff's ratio: the reported figure is lower than 3.58 times, and the cause (treatment of junior subordinated notes and preferred, pro forma EBITDA, which debt is included) is Not supplied. Sunoco LP's credit facility requires "a specified net leverage ratio and interest coverage ratio" and USAC's credit facility has its own covenants; their levels are Not supplied (10-K page:330). The issuer states that it and its subsidiaries were "in compliance with all requirements, tests, limitations and covenants" at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:18).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Energy Transfer LP is a large, diversified midstream operator whose eight reportable segments cover natural gas gathering, processing and transportation, NGL and refined products, crude oil, and two publicly traded consolidated subsidiaries: Sunoco LP (fuel distribution and terminals) and USAC (compression). The 10-K states that no customer individually accounted for more than 10 percent of revenue in FY2025, and in Q3 2026 no segment contributed more than a quarter of Adjusted EBITDA on the figures in CP-1, so concentration risk by customer or segment is limited on the documents read. The creditor-relevant features are three. First, change: Sunoco LP acquired Parkland on October 31, 2025, which enlarged that segment's revenue and earnings (it supplied 560 US$m of the 1,193 US$m increase in Q3 Adjusted EBITDA in CP-1) and added subsidiary debt, so the reported leverage improvement depends on a subsidiary with separate creditors. Second, a continuing programme of acquisitions and growth capital: J-W Power, TanQuid, Delta and Offen in 2026, Vaquero agreed on October 6, 2026 for about 2.63 billion US$ (1.95 billion US$ cash plus about 33.3 million new common units), growth capital guided at 5.4 billion to 5.6 billion US$ for 2026 and about 7 billion US$ for 2027. Third, structure and control: the parent's senior notes are unguaranteed by subsidiaries, a single individual controls the general partner, and the issuer's state of organisation and exchange changed in 2026 without a supplied explanation.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: no customer above 10 percent of revenue (10-K page:39); demand-fee and take-or-pay contracts (10-K page:8 and page:11). Mechanic: contracted fee streams cover a share of margin, while marketing, processing margins and fuel distribution vary with commodity spreads. Implication: earnings are more stable than the product-sales revenue suggests, but the proportion of margin that is contracted is Not supplied, so the coverage of fixed charges by contracted income cannot be stated. Counter-evidence: working capital and unrealized commodity swings in cash flow (CP-1). 2. Subsidiary leverage and structural subordination. Evidence: separate Sunoco LP and USAC facilities and notes, and parent notes unguaranteed (10-K page:325; Q3 10-Q page:18). Mechanic: subsidiary creditors rank ahead of the parent in subsidiary assets and cash, while Sunoco LP supplied 560 US$m of the Q3 Adjusted EBITDA increase (CP-1). Implication: the parent's creditors benefit from growth in those subsidiaries only through distributions, so parent leverage measured on consolidated EBITDA overstates parent-available coverage; this is a consideration for CP-2, not a conclusion. 3. Acquisition-led growth and funding. Evidence: Vaquero, Offen, J-W Power, TanQuid and Parkland (Q3 10-Q page:57 and page:58; 10-K page:313). Mechanic: cash components add to borrowings or draw on facilities; unit components dilute distributions per unit. Implication: leverage tolerance depends on EBITDA growth outpacing debt; the Vaquero funding plan is Not supplied, so pro forma leverage is Not calculable. 4. Control and governance. Evidence: 81.2 percent of the general partner and all Class A units (10-K page:132); derivative litigation (Q3 10-Q page:32). Mechanic: unitholders cannot remove the general partner without the vote described, and creditors have no governance rights. Implication: monitoring posture should rest on covenants and disclosure; the partnership agreement is Not supplied. 5. Identity and listing change. Evidence: cover pages and 8-K12B reference. Mechanic: a change of state of organisation could alter the obligor, the governing documents or successor language. Implication: structural analysis should wait for the filing; the conflict logged below counters any assumption of continuity. 6. Key uncertainties: breakdown of contracted versus commodity-linked margin, Vaquero funding, covenant definitions, hybrid treatment, litigation outcomes (Dakota Access and others), and the 8-K12B.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Energy Transfer's debt looks serviceable on current earnings and liquidity, but it depends on subsidiary earnings growth and continued market access. The strongest support is scale and diversity: USD 19,216 million of LTM Adjusted EBITDA across eight segments, no customer above 10 percent of revenue, and USD 8,692 million of cash and undrawn facilities. The weakest point is that free cash flow does not cover distributions and growth capital, so leverage of 3.58x (4.28x for FY2025) rests on earnings growth, much of it from Sunoco LP, and on refinancing about USD 4,350 million due by September 30, 2027. Covenant terms, the 2026 change of state and the Vaquero funding plan decide whether the view holds.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage has eased through earnings, not repayment. Total debt was USD 68,850 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 68,333 million at December 31, 2025, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 19,216 million from USD 15,984 million, which moves total debt over Adjusted EBITDA from 4.28x to 3.58x and net debt from 4.20x to 3.53x [financial base: leverage and coverage]. Nine months of 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 15,034 million compares with USD 11,802 million, and the Sunoco LP segment supplied USD 560 million of the USD 1,193 million Q3 increase [financial base: reported results; business context: operating model]. The issuer's covenant leverage ratio under the Five-Year Credit Facility was 2.83x against a maximum of 5.00x (5.50x in a Specified Acquisition Period), so on the issuer's own basis headroom is 2.17 turns, which would allow Adjusted EBITDA to fall by about 43.4 percent at constant debt (Calculations C1) [financial base: leverage and coverage]. The covenant definition is not supplied and gives a lower ratio than the simple one, so the headroom is indicative only.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings quality needs care. Adjusted EBITDA is an issuer non-GAAP measure that for nine months 2026 adds back USD 519 million of unrealized commodity losses, removes USD 445 million of inventory valuation gains and includes USD 588 million of Adjusted EBITDA of unconsolidated affiliates [financial base: reconciliation]. On operating income plus depreciation, depletion and amortization, total debt is 3.90x LTM against 4.65x for FY2025, so the improving direction survives a GAAP cross-check, but the level is higher than the covenant figure. Revenue of USD 124,528 million LTM is mostly pass-through product sales (fees were 14.5 percent of FY2025 revenue), so margin analysis must use Adjusted EBITDA [business context: operating model].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash flow covers interest but not distributions plus growth capital. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid 5.43x LTM and interest expense 5.14x; interest expense takes 19.4 percent of LTM Adjusted EBITDA (Calculations C2) [financial base: leverage and coverage]. LTM operating cash flow of USD 13,569 million less capital expenditure of USD 7,487 million leaves free cash flow of USD 6,082 million, below distributions of USD 6,955 million to partners and noncontrolling interests, a shortfall of USD 873 million that arose in the fourth quarter of 2025 [financial base: cash flow quality]. On the issuer's own Distributable Cash Flow basis, which excludes growth capital, the partnership is close to self-funding: for nine months 2026, Distributable Cash Flow attributable to partners, as adjusted, of USD 7,813 million covered distributions of USD 3,515 million 2.22x and left USD 4,298 million against accrual-basis growth capital of USD 4,432 million, a gap of USD 134 million (Calculations C3; Q3 release page:8, Q3 10-Q page:86). Growth capital is guided at USD 5.4 billion to USD 5.6 billion for 2026 and about USD 7 billion for 2027 [business context: operating model], so the partnership will keep relying on debt and subsidiary-level capital.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The near-term maturity wall is smaller at the parent than CP-1 implied. The issuer states that about USD 4,350 million of principal due on or before September 30, 2027 is classed as long-term on refinancing intent and ability (Q3 10-Q page:88). Adding the instruments in the December 31, 2025 table that mature by that date and were not redeemed in 2026 gives USD 3,300 million at the parent (6.05% notes of USD 1,000 million due December 1, 2026; 4.40% notes of USD 700 million; 4.20% notes of USD 600 million; and two 5.50% notes due June 1, 2027 of USD 44 million and USD 956 million) and USD 1,050 million at Sunoco LP (5.625% and 5.875% notes due 2027, 550, 499 and 1), which sums to USD 4,350 million (Calculations C4; 10-K page:322). This is an Analyst Interpretation: the footnote does not split the amount and the 2027 months for the Sunoco LP notes are not printed. It corrects the CP-1 sentence that compared the whole USD 4,350 million with the parent's USD 4,406 million of availability: that comparison overstates the parent's need, though the parent still has USD 3,300 million to refinance within about eleven months, including USD 1,000 million on December 1, 2026, which is within a month of the as-of date.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Structure matters for the parent's creditors. The parent's notes and debentures plus Five-Year Credit Facility are USD 52,035 million of principal and its senior notes are not guaranteed by subsidiaries; Sunoco LP and USAC together carry USD 16,276 million with separate facilities [financial base: debt and capital structure; business context: ownership and capital allocation]. As an indicative proxy, parent principal over LTM Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Sunoco LP and USAC segments (USD 14,946 million) is 3.48x (Calculations C5). That proxy ignores the cash distributions the parent receives from them (Sunoco LP USD 306 million and USAC USD 73 million for nine months 2026 on the Distributable Cash Flow basis, Q3 release page:7) and counts non-wholly-owned joint ventures at 100 percent, so it shows only that excluding the subsidiaries does not make parent leverage lower than the consolidated figure of 3.58x by much. Whether parent-level coverage is adequate cannot be tested without parent-only statements, which are not supplied.

facts.text: Acquisitions and control are the main forward risks. Vaquero (total consideration about USD 2.63 billion, USD 1.95 billion in cash) is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 and Offen (about USD 600 million) closed on October 27, 2026 at Sunoco LP; the cash consideration for Vaquero equals 44.3 percent of the parent's revolver availability, and the funding plan is Not supplied [business context: transaction summary]. Contingent matters are moderate against EBITDA: accruals of USD 536 million, additional reasonably possible losses up to approximately USD 76 million, and unrecorded favourable verdicts of approximately USD 795 million in aggregate, of which USD 393 million was recorded in October 2026 [business context: operating model and timeline].

facts.text: Strengths. (1) Scale and diversity: eight segments, no customer above 10 percent of revenue and a largest segment of 24.3 percent of Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA, which limits single-asset or single-customer risk (Documentary Fact; business context). (2) Earnings momentum and conversion: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 19,216 million, raised 2026 guidance of USD 19.7 billion to USD 19.9 billion, and Distributable Cash Flow covering distributions 2.22x for nine months (Documentary Fact for the figures; guidance is Management Language). (3) Liquidity: USD 8,692 million including subsidiary facilities, USD 4,406 million at the parent, and revolver extended to 2029 (Documentary Fact; financial base). (4) Demonstrated market access: USD 3,000 million of senior notes in January 2026 and USD 1,750 million of junior subordinated notes in July 2026, with USD 4,350 million of near-term maturities classed as refinanceable (Documentary Fact). (5) Covenant headroom on the issuer's reported basis of 2.17 turns (Documentary Fact for the figures; the headroom is an Analyst Interpretation).

rows.label: Energy Transfer's debt looks serviceable on current earnings and liquidity, with leverage of 3.58 times easing from 4.28 times, but it depends on subsidiary earnings growth, continued market access and funding for acquisitions.
Total debt over LTM Adjusted EBITDA fell to 3.58 times from 4.28 times, while the reported covenant leverage ratio was 2.83 times against a 5.00 times limit.
Free cash flow of USD 6,082 million fell USD 873 million short of distributions over the last twelve months.
About USD 4,350 million of principal is due by September 30, 2027, of which about USD 3,300 million is at the parent.
The parent's USD 52,035 million of principal is unguaranteed and Sunoco LP and USAC carry USD 16,276 million with their own facilities.
Vaquero adds USD 1,950 million of cash consideration and Offen about USD 600 million at Sunoco LP, with funding not stated.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and releases are enough to run the four requested modules with stated limits. Statements, debt notes, liquidity and the latest quarter are all located; indentures, credit agreements and the corporate conversion documents are not. | Medium | Executed debt documents and the filing that records the change of corporate form are not supplied, so covenant terms and guarantor structure rest on filing summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Audited year-end statements and three quarterly reports are all present, and the latest quarterly report is dated on the as-of date. | Current-period work can use filed, controlling statements without gaps in the quarter sequence. | High |

| The issuer's form and listing changed during 2026, but the supplied files only show this on cover pages and in one cross-reference. | The legal entity that owns the debt should be confirmed before any structural conclusion. | Medium |

| Debt sits at the parent and at two publicly traded subsidiaries, each with its own facilities. | A single consolidated debt figure mixes parent and subsidiary obligations; later work must keep them apart. | Medium |
| Earnings releases are management presentations and repeat the quarterly reports. | They add non-GAAP measures and guidance but cannot override the filings. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set supports all four requested modules with limitations. The company's annual report, its three 2026 quarterly reports and its three earnings releases carry consistent period labels and the same commission file number, differing only in state of organisation and listing venue (see Identity and perimeter), and together cover the full fiscal year 2025, the nine months to September 30, 2026 and the events up to the as-of date. Source sufficiency is established for statements, the debt note, liquidity text, segments and subsequent events. It is not established for executed debt agreements, indentures, or the filing that records the change of corporate form, none of which is supplied. This is a source verdict only; completion of downstream analysis is not asserted.
| Consumer | Status | Basis |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Audited FY2025 statements, interim statements for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 with comparatives, debt tables and segment note are located. Source text is a flattened HTML extraction, so table layout was not visually checked. |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, segments, subsidiary structure, acquisitions and the October 2026 Vaquero agreement are located. The change in jurisdiction and exchange listing is evidenced only on cover pages and one cross-reference; the underlying filing is not supplied. |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Debt tables, credit facility availability, the stated covenant leverage ratio and subsidiary facilities are located. Credit agreement and indenture definitions are not supplied, so the covenant ratio cannot be rebuilt from definitions. |
| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every source is page-chunked and traceable. No original HTML, XBRL or images are supplied; visual and chart checks are not possible. |
Command sheet: CP-1 RUN; CP-1A RUN; CP-2 RUN; CP-5 RUN.
### Source register

- Family and authority: filed annual report and original authority for audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements. page:1 reads "For the fiscal year ended DECEMBER 31, 2025" and "Commission file number 1-32740".

- Audit: page:283 holds the report of the independent registered public accounting firm ("We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Energy Transfer LP (a Delaware limited partnership)"). The internal-control opinion is signed "GRANT THORNTON LLP Dallas, Texas February 19, 2026" (page:229).

- Statements: balance sheet at page:286 and page:287; statements of operations at page:287 and page:288; cash flows at page:288 and page:289. Debt note tables at page:323 and page:324, with text on notes and the credit facility from page:325. Reportable segments note at page:394. The index to financial statements is at page:282.
- Perimeter: consolidated Energy Transfer LP and subsidiaries, with noncontrolling interests. At filing, the cover shows state "Delaware" and exchange "New York Stock Exchange" (page:1).
- Units: dollars in millions unless stated; USD.
#### Form 10-Q, quarter ended March 31, 2026 (`10-Q_2026-03-31_et-20260331.htm.jsonl`)
- Family and authority: filed, unaudited interim report. page:1 reads "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026"; signature page:83 "Date: May 7, 2026".
- Debt table with March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025 columns at page:72 ("Total debt 69,336 68,333").
- Cover state is "Delaware" (page:1).
#### Form 10-Q, quarter ended June 30, 2026 (`10-Q_2026-06-30_et-20260630.htm.jsonl`)
- Family and authority: filed, unaudited interim report. page:1 reads "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026"; signature page:95 "Date: August 6, 2026".
- Debt table at page:84 ("Total debt 68,405 68,333").
- Cover state is "Texas" while the listing is still "New York Stock Exchange" (page:1). The state of incorporation therefore differs from the 10-K and first-quarter report.
#### Form 10-Q, quarter ended September 30, 2026 (`10-Q_2026-09-30_et-20260930.htm.jsonl`)

- Family and authority: filed, unaudited interim report and the controlling source for the latest period. page:1 reads "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026"; signature page:99 "Date: November 5, 2026", which is the as-of date. It is inside the cutoff.

- Statements: balance sheet page:3 and page:4 (cash "Cash and cash equivalents $ 926 $ 1,272"), statements of operations page:4 and page:5, equity page:6, cash flows page:6 and page:7. Note 7 debt at page:17 and page:18; debt table at page:87; segment note 13 at page:52; Management's Discussion from page:57; liquidity from page:83.

- Cover state "Texas" and exchange "Texas Stock Exchange" for both the common units and the Series I preferred units (page:1). The MD&A refers to a "Current Report on Form 8-K12B filed with the SEC on July 6, 2026" (page:57). That current report is not supplied.
#### Earnings releases, Exhibit 99.1 (three files)

- Family and authority: issuer press releases furnished as exhibits: first quarter "Dallas – May 5, 2026", second quarter "Dallas – August 4, 2026", third quarter "Dallas – November 3, 2026" (page:2 of each). Management-prepared and unaudited; they present reported and non-GAAP measures.
- The first two releases label the listing "NYSE:ET" and the third labels it "TXSE:ET" (page:2 of each), matching the cover pages of the 10-Qs.

- Content located in the third-quarter release: condensed balance sheet (page:6), statement of operations (page:6, page:7), reconciliation of net income to Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow (page:7), segment discussion (page:12 to page:17), liquidity table (page:17), unconsolidated affiliates (page:17) and non-wholly owned subsidiaries (page:18). Guidance: "The Partnership now expects its Adjusted EBITDA for the full year of 2026 to range between $19.7 billion and $19.9 billion" (page:2).

- Version relationship: the statement of operations and balance sheet repeat the 10-Q for the same period. The 10-Q controls for statement facts; the release is attributed management presentation for Adjusted EBITDA, Distributable Cash Flow and guidance. The release is not independent corroboration of the 10-Q statements.
- The release liquidity table shows only the parent facility: "We also have consolidated subsidiaries with revolving credit facilities which are not included in this table." (page:17)
### Information-availability boundary
- Latest supplied document is the Form 10-Q signed November 5, 2026, the as-of date. Nothing is dated after the cutoff.

- Events between the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date and November 5, 2026 are limited to what the 10-Q and the third-quarter release state, for example the acquisition agreement signed on "October 6, 2026" for Vaquero (10-Q page:57) and the termination on "October 8, 2026" of Sunoco LP's receivables financing agreement (10-Q page:18). Other post-quarter filings, such as current reports, are Not supplied, not absent.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Energy Transfer LP, Dallas, Texas. The filings describe the Partnership as consolidating Sunoco LP, USAC and SunocoCorp (10-Q Q3 page:8, "The Partnership owns a controlling interest in USAC.").

- Subsidiary debt: the Q3 10-Q note on debt names separate facilities for Sunoco LP ("Sunoco LP Credit Facility") and USAC ("USAC Credit Facility") in addition to the parent's "Five-Year Credit Facility" (page:18), and the Q3 debt table at page:87 lists them as separate lines. These are consolidated but separate borrowers.

- Notes at the parent: the 10-K states "The Energy Transfer senior notes are not guaranteed by any of its subsidiaries." (page:325). Guarantor structure for other instruments is not stated in the supplied text; the context leaves borrower, parent and guarantor fields blank, which is not evidence of their absence.

- Change of form and listing: the 10-K cover shows Delaware and the New York Stock Exchange; the first-quarter report shows Delaware; the second-quarter report shows Texas with the New York Stock Exchange; the third-quarter report shows Texas with the Texas Stock Exchange. The files do not describe the transaction that caused this, apart from the 8-K12B cross-reference. Whether the registrant is the same legal entity, a successor, and whether indenture and credit agreement parties changed is an unresolved distinction carried as a gap. The commission file number is unchanged at "1-32740" on all four periodic reports (page:1 of each).
- Preferred units: "9.250% Series I Fixed Rate Perpetual Preferred Units" are listed with the common units (page:1 of the Q3 10-Q).
### Consumer evidence demand

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, debt, liquidity, non-GAAP, nine-month and quarter columns | 10-K page:286 to page:289 and page:323 to page:324; Q3 10-Q page:3 to page:7, page:17 to page:18, page:87; Q3 release page:6 to page:7 | Flattened text; Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow are issuer non-GAAP; consolidated debt includes subsidiary debt |

| CP-1A | Business, segments, subsidiaries, acquisitions, ownership, recent developments | 10-K page:394; Q3 10-Q page:8, page:52, page:57; Q3 release page:2 to page:4 | Change of state and exchange documented only on covers; Vaquero closing is a post-quarter expectation |

| CP-2 | Debt by issuer, maturities, facilities, covenant statement, liquidity, commitments | 10-K page:323 to page:325; Q3 10-Q page:18, page:83 to page:89 | Credit agreements and indentures not supplied; covenant ratio is as reported, not rebuildable |
| CP-5 | Traceable claims | All seven sources are chunked with stable page numbers | No HTML, XBRL or images; chunk numbers are not printed page numbers |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: the 10-K gives audited FY2025 and prior-year comparatives; the three 10-Qs give Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 with comparatives and a nine-month cash flow statement in the latest report. Together they allow discrete quarters to be derived later and a last-twelve-months view to be built from the year and the nine-month periods. This is a statement of source sufficiency; the derivation itself is not performed here.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the issuer changed state of organisation and listing venue mid-year, and the files give only cover-page evidence and the 8-K12B cross-reference. If the registrant, obligor or indenture parties changed, a consumer that treats the FY2025 audited entity as identical to the Q3 2026 entity could misattribute debt and covenants.

- Source risk mechanism: reported debt combines the parent's notes and facilities with those of Sunoco LP and USAC, which have their own revolvers and note series and are not guaranteed by the parent's notes. A consumer that reads only a consolidated debt total can overstate the parent's own claim stack or understate the subsidiary-level priority.

- Second mechanism: management's Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow in the releases are reconciled to net income but include items such as Adjusted EBITDA of unconsolidated affiliates; they are not audited and the covenant leverage ratio in the 10-Q is defined in agreements that are not supplied.

- What cannot proceed: covenant rebuilds from agreement definitions, guarantor-by-guarantor analysis, legal entity mapping across the change of form, and any use of market, ratings or peer data (none supplied, context lists none).

- Next evidence action: supply the Form 8-K12B filed on July 6, 2026 and the related successor documentation, the current revolving credit agreement and indentures for the parent senior and junior subordinated notes, and any current reports dated after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date up to November 5, 2026.
## Calculations
No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Figures that appear above are quoted from the cited locators for identification only.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |
| Form 8-K12B filed July 6, 2026 and documents of the change of state and listing not supplied | High | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the filing and any successor-obligor or supplemental indenture documents |

| Executed credit agreement, indentures and supplemental indentures not supplied; covenant definitions and guarantor lists not verifiable | High for legal work; Medium for CP-2 | CP-2 | Supply executed documents |
| Current reports and other filings between the Q3 balance sheet date and November 5, 2026 not supplied | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply or confirm none |
| Flattened HTML text only; tables not visually checked, no XBRL, no images or charts | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Check flagged tables against the filed HTML |
| Releases are management non-GAAP presentations; Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow are not audited | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Label as issuer non-GAAP; rely on the 10-Q for statement facts |

| Subsidiary credit facilities and note series sit inside consolidated debt; guarantor structure beyond the parent senior notes statement not located | Medium | CP-2 | Keep parent and subsidiary debt separate; seek subsidiary debt documents if needed |
| No rating reports, market prices, peer or valuation data (context fields blank) | Low for the selected modules | CP-2 | Not required for this scope; keep Not supplied |
## Next module

- CP-1: treat the 10-K and the 10-Qs as controlling for statements; keep audited annual, quarter and nine-month columns separate; keep parent and subsidiary debt separate; label Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow from the releases as issuer non-GAAP; use the Q3 10-Q as the latest balance sheet.

- CP-1A: carry the change of state and exchange as an unresolved identity point with only cover-page evidence; carry the Vaquero acquisition as signed on October 6, 2026 and not closed; treat anything after November 5, 2026 as outside the cutoff.
- CP-2 and CP-5: carry the missing executed debt documents and the 8-K12B as restrictions; do not rebuild the covenant ratio from definitions; cite by file and page chunk.

Current period Q3 2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026); prior period FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025). ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Debt of 68,850 US$m is 3.58 times LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 19,216 US$m, down from 4.28 times at year-end, with 7,766 US$m of undrawn facilities across the parent and two listed subsidiaries. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is issuer non-GAAP, covenant definitions are not supplied, and maturities are only available as at year-end. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Adjusted EBITDA rose to 5,031 US$m in Q3 2026 from 3,838 US$m, with the Sunoco LP segment adding 560 US$m of the 1,193 US$m increase. | Leverage falls mainly through earnings growth, much of it in a fuel-distribution subsidiary with its own creditors, not through lower debt. | Medium |

| Total debt rose by 517 US$m in nine months to 68,850 US$m while about 4,350 US$m due by September 30, 2027 is classed as long-term. | Refinancing depends on continued market access and the revolver, although the issuer reports covenant leverage of 2.83 times. | Medium |

| Free cash flow after capital expenditure was 6,082 US$m over the last twelve months but fell short of distributions to partners and noncontrolling interest holders by 873 US$m. | Growth capital and distributions rely on borrowing and capital markets access. | Medium |
| Liquidity is 8,692 US$m of cash and undrawn facilities, of which only 4,406 US$m is at the parent. | The remainder is at Sunoco LP and USAC, which are separate borrowers. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is adequate for a credit snapshot, with the limits stated here. On the printed statements, consolidated debt was 68,850 US$m at September 30, 2026 against 68,333 US$m at December 31, 2025, cash was 926 US$m, and Adjusted EBITDA (issuer non-GAAP, consolidated) for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 19,216 US$m, built as FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025. Total debt over that EBITDA is 3.58 times, against 4.28 times for FY2025 and 4.12 times on the March 31, 2026 LTM. The improvement is driven by earnings: Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 is 15,034 US$m against 11,802 US$m, while debt rose. The issuer's own covenant leverage ratio, calculated under a definition not supplied, was 2.83 times at September 30, 2026 and 3.21 times at December 31, 2025, so the covenant basis is lower than the simple ratio at both dates (by 1.07 turns at year-end and 0.75 turns at September 30, 2026, C9). Interest cover on Adjusted EBITDA over cash interest paid is 5.43 times LTM, with cash interest approximated from nine-month figures printed in billions.

Three features limit how far the headline can be read. First, the perimeter mixes the parent's debt (notes and debentures, the Five-Year Credit Facility) with that of Sunoco LP (13,131 US$m of senior notes, bonds and lease-related obligations plus a 111 US$m facility) and USAC (2,350 US$m of senior notes plus a 684 US$m facility), each with separate facilities and creditors; Adjusted EBITDA is consolidated at 100 percent, with 15,209 US$m of noncontrolling interests outside partners' capital. Second, earnings quality: the nine-month 2026 reconciliation adds back 519 US$m of unrealized commodity losses and removes 445 US$m of inventory valuation gains, and Q3 revenue was 37,103 US$m against 19,954 US$m, concentrated in fuel sales of the Sunoco LP segment, so margins are not comparable year on year. Third, claims outside debt (operating leases of 1,862 US$m, preferred units of 2,480 US$m, redeemable noncontrolling interests of 266 US$m, contingent accruals of 536 US$m) and the pending Vaquero acquisition (1.95 billion US$ cash plus about 33.3 million common units) are outside the leverage figures.
### Reporting entity, periods and definitions
| Source | Entity and perimeter | Periods | Statement kind | Units |

| 10-K | Energy Transfer LP and subsidiaries, consolidated, with noncontrolling interests | Years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023; balance sheets at December 31, 2025 and 2024 | Audited (Grant Thornton LLP, report dated February 19, 2026, 10-K page:283 and page:286) | "(Dollars in millions)" (page:286); USD |

| Q1 10-Q, Q2 10-Q, Q3 10-Q | Same consolidated perimeter | Three and, for Q3, nine months to the quarter end, with comparatives; balance sheet at quarter end and December 31, 2025 | Unaudited | "(Dollars in millions)" (Q3 10-Q page:3); USD |
| Releases (three) | Same perimeter, issuer presentation | Quarter and year-to-date | Unaudited, non-GAAP | Millions; USD |

Definitions: Adjusted EBITDA is defined by the issuer as "total partnership earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, depletion, amortization and other non-cash items" with further listed adjustments, including Adjusted EBITDA related to unconsolidated affiliates (Q3 release page:9). It is not audited. "Total debt" in this handoff is the printed total on the debt table (carrying value, after premiums, discounts and issuance costs), not principal. Net debt is that total less cash and cash equivalents; restricted cash is not shown separately in the sources. LTM means FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025, and is labelled wherever used. Ratios are not covenant ratios.

Balance sheet items are instants (period end). Flows have durations: Q3 is July 1 to September 30; nine months is January 1 to September 30. The Sunoco LP credit facility, USAC credit facility and the parent's Five-Year Credit Facility are separate borrowers.
### Reported results

Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:4): total revenues 37,103 against 19,954; operating income 2,781 against 2,151; net income 1,814 against 1,292; net income attributable to partners 1,207 against 1,019. Nine months 2026 against 2025: revenues 99,208 against 60,216; operating income 9,338 against 6,951; net income 6,320 against 4,470.

The 10-Q attributes the Q3 increase "primarily" to higher segment margin in the intrastate transportation and storage segment (Hugh Brinson Pipeline early volumes), the midstream segment, and Sunoco LP and USAC where "segment margin increased due to recent acquisitions" (Q3 10-Q page:68). The revenue step-up is concentrated in the Sunoco LP segment: segment revenues 18,029 in Q3 2026 against 6,032 in Q3 2025, and 42,978 against 16,601 for nine months (Q3 10-Q page:53). Refined product sales were 17,577 in Q3 2026 against 5,849 (page:4).

### Debt and capital structure
Consolidated debt as printed in the Q3 10-Q (page:87), carrying basis, with the principal subtotal calculated (C4):
| Instrument group (as printed) | September 30, 2026 | December 31, 2025 | Issuer or borrower |
| Notes and debentures | 51,470 | 48,870 | Energy Transfer LP (parent) |
| Five-Year Credit Facility | 565 | 2,856 | Energy Transfer LP (parent) |
| Transwestern senior notes | 75 | 75 | Transwestern Pipeline (subsidiary) |
| Bakken Project senior notes | 850 | 850 | Bakken Project (subsidiary) |
| Sunoco LP senior notes, bonds and lease-related obligations | 13,131 | 13,470 | Sunoco LP (subsidiary) |
| USAC senior notes | 2,350 | 1,750 | USAC (subsidiary) |
| Sunoco LP credit facility | 111 | — | Sunoco LP |
| USAC credit facility | 684 | 795 | USAC |
| Other long-term debt | 15 | 19 | Various |
| Principal subtotal (calculated, C4) | 69,251 | 68,685 | |
| Net unamortized premiums, discounts and fair value adjustments | 12 | 32 | |

| Total debt (printed) | 68,850 | 68,333 | |

| Long-term debt, less current maturities | 68,838 | 68,308 | |

The parent's claim is notes and debentures plus the Five-Year Credit Facility: 52,035 US$m of principal at September 30, 2026 (C4), about three quarters of the total. Sunoco LP and USAC together account for 16,276 US$m of principal (13,131 + 111 + 2,350 + 684, C4). Footnote (1) to the table states that "approximately $4.35 billion aggregate principal amount due on or before September 30, 2027" is classified long-term because management has "the intent and ability to refinance the borrowings on a long-term basis" (Q3 10-Q page:88), so current maturities of 12 understate near-term refinancing.

Structure points from the filings: the Energy Transfer senior notes "are not guaranteed by any of its subsidiaries" (10-K page:325). The Dec 31, 2025 table (10-K page:322 to page:324) shows five parent junior subordinated issues totalling 3,800 (8.00% due 2054 at 800, 7.125% due 2054 at 400, Series 2025A at 1,200, Series 2025B at 800, floating rate due 2066 at 600; C5). In July 2026 the parent issued a further 650 (Series 2026A, 6.550% initially) and 1,100 (Series 2026B, 6.700% initially) of junior subordinated notes due 2057, used "to redeem the Series H Preferred Units, to repay borrowings under its Five-Year Credit Facility and for general partnership purposes" (Q3 10-Q page:17). Junior subordinated notes at the parent are therefore 5,550 in principal at September 30, 2026 on these figures (C5), a calculated amount: the Q3 10-Q does not print an instrument table. Whether they carry equity treatment for rating or covenant purposes is Not supplied.

Debt movements in 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:17 and page:88 to page:89): parent issued 1,000 of 4.55% notes due 2031, 1,000 of 5.35% due 2036 and 1,000 of 6.30% due 2056 in January; redeemed 1,000 of 4.75% notes due January 2026, 600 of 5.625% notes due May 2027 and 550 of 3.90% notes due July 2026. Sunoco LP issued 600 of 5.375% notes due 2031 and 600 of 5.625% notes due 2034 and redeemed 500 and 600 of 6.000% notes due 2026 and 2027; it also redeemed its 3.875% CAD notes due 2026 (June) and 6.000% CAD notes due 2028 (August). USAC issued 600 of 6.750% senior notes due 2035 in September. The cash flow statement shows borrowings of 26,320 and repayments of 26,089 for nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:7), a net increase of 231 that the MD&A also states (page:87); total debt rose by 517 over the same period on the printed totals (C4), the difference being non-cash movements such as notes assumed or foreign exchange and premiums that this handoff does not break down.

Maturity profile. The most recent maturity table is at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:324): 2026 3,512; 2027 5,314; 2028 4,505; 2029 11,619; 2030 6,154; thereafter 37,581; total 68,685, which agrees with the principal subtotal above (C3). The 2026 and part of the 2027 maturities have since been redeemed or refinanced as listed above, but no later table is printed in the Q1, Q2 or Q3 10-Q, so the maturity chart below is on a December 31, 2025 basis and is stale for those years. The 2029 bucket is the largest at 11,619 and includes the Five-Year Credit Facility (2,856 drawn) because it matures April 11, 2029.
Facilities (revolving, committed):
| Facility | Size and maturity | Drawn and letters of credit | Available | Date and source |

| Energy Transfer Five-Year Credit Facility | 5,000 until April 11, 2027, then 4,840 until April 11, 2029 | 565 drawn, of which 441 commercial paper; letters of credit 29 | 4,410 printed in billions; 4,406 in the release | September 30, 2026; Q3 10-Q page:18; Q3 release page:17 |
| Sunoco LP Credit Facility | 2,500, matures June 2030 | 111 drawn; standby letters of credit 84 | 2,300 | September 30, 2026; Q3 10-Q page:18; size from 10-K page:328 |
| USAC Credit Facility | Matures August 2030 | 684 drawn; letters of credit 2 | 1,060 | September 30, 2026; Q3 10-Q page:18 |

The 10-Q states the Five-Year Credit Facility "allows for unsecured borrowings up to $5.00 billion until April 11, 2027, and up to $4.84 billion until April 11, 2029" (Q3 10-Q page:18), so commitments step down by 160 on April 11, 2027, which is within twelve months of the as-of date. Sunoco LP's NuStar receivables financing agreement had no borrowings at September 30, 2026 and was terminated on October 8, 2026 (page:18).
### Liquidity
Liquidity by facility at each balance sheet date, calculated as cash plus undrawn availability as printed (C6):
| Date | Cash | Parent facility available | Sunoco LP facility available | USAC facility available | Total |

Sources: balance sheets (10-K page:286; Q1 10-Q page:3; Q2 10-Q page:3; Q3 10-Q page:3) and facility text (10-K page:328 and page:209; Q1 10-Q page:14; Q2 10-Q page:17; Q3 10-Q page:18). Availability is stated by the issuer net of letters of credit. Cash is consolidated cash and includes cash at Sunoco LP and USAC; a split of cash by borrower is Not supplied. Restricted cash is Not supplied as a separate line. Commercial paper of 441 is issued under the parent facility and reduces the parent availability shown; no separate commercial paper backstop is added.

Near-term demands: the approximately 4,350 of principal due by September 30, 2027 is close to the parent availability of 4,406, so the parent revolver is not enough by itself for that wall without market refinancing. The commitment step-down in April 2027 and planned growth capital ("$5.4 billion to $5.6 billion in growth capital for 2026 and approximately $7 billion for 2027", Q3 release page:2) add to uses. The Vaquero cash consideration of 1.95 billion US$ and the Offen acquisition by Sunoco LP of about 600 (completed October 27, 2026, Q3 10-Q page:58) are after the balance sheet date and are not in the table.
### Cash flow quality
Cash flow statements (10-K page:289 and page:290; Q3 10-Q page:6 and page:7):
| Line (as printed) | FY2025 | Nine months 2026 | Nine months 2025 | LTM (C7) |
| Net cash provided by operating activities | 10,149 | 11,671 | 8,251 | 13,569 |
| Capital expenditures, excluding allowance for equity funds used during construction | (6,303) | (5,364) | (4,180) | (7,487) |
| Free cash flow, calculated | 3,846 | 6,307 | 4,071 | 6,082 |
| Distributions to partners | (4,725) | (3,611) | (3,504) | (4,832) |
| Distributions to noncontrolling interests | (1,734) | (1,658) | (1,310) | (2,082) |
| Distributions to redeemable noncontrolling interests | (56) | (30) | (45) | (41) |
| Net change in operating assets and liabilities | (1,976) | 784 | (483) | (709) |
| Proceeds from borrowings | 32,870 | 26,320 | 26,875 | 32,315 |

Reading: operating cash flow for nine months 2026 exceeds the prior nine months by 3,420 (calculated, C7), partly because working capital turned from an outflow of 483 to an inflow of 784. FY2025 operating cash flow of 10,149 was reduced by a 1,976 working capital outflow. LTM free cash flow of 6,082 is not enough to cover the LTM distributions of 4,832 to partners, 2,082 to noncontrolling interests and 41 to redeemable noncontrolling interests, which total 6,955 and leave a shortfall of 873 (C7). The nine months 2026 alone cover them (6,307 less 5,299 of distributions is 1,008, C7), so the LTM shortfall comes from the fourth quarter of 2025, when capital expenditure of 2,123 exceeded operating cash flow of 1,898 (C7). Cash paid for interest, net of interest capitalized, was 3,136 in FY2025 (10-K page:294), and "$2.45 billion and $2.05 billion" for nine months 2026 and 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:85); interest capitalized was 174 against 98 for the nine months (page:85). The cash flow statement shows the nine-month 2026 ending cash of 926 against 3,574 a year earlier (page:7).
### Leverage and coverage
Calculated, with Adjusted EBITDA on an LTM basis at each date (C8). Total debt is the printed total (carrying value).
| Date | LTM Adjusted EBITDA | Total debt | Cash | Total debt / EBITDA | Net debt / EBITDA |

Issuer-reported covenant leverage under the Five-Year Credit Facility: 3.21 to 1.00 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:330), 3.16 times for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:14), 3.01 times at June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:17) and 2.83 times at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:18). The facility "limits us, on a rolling four quarter basis, to a maximum Consolidated Funded Indebtedness to Consolidated EBITDA ratio, as defined in the underlying credit agreement, of 5.00 to 1.00, which can generally be increased to 5.50 to 1.00 during a Specified Acquisition Period" (10-K page:330). The headroom against the 5.00 to 1.00 limit is therefore 2.17 turns on the reported 2.83 times (calculated, C9), before any Specified Acquisition Period increase. The covenant definition differs from this handoff's ratio: the reported figure is lower than 3.58 times, and the cause (treatment of junior subordinated notes and preferred, pro forma EBITDA, which debt is included) is Not supplied. Sunoco LP's credit facility requires "a specified net leverage ratio and interest coverage ratio" and USAC's credit facility has its own covenants; their levels are Not supplied (10-K page:330). The issuer states that it and its subsidiaries were "in compliance with all requirements, tests, limitations and covenants" at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:18).

Coverage (calculated, C10): Adjusted EBITDA over interest expense, net of interest capitalized, is 5.14 times LTM (19,216 over 3,735) and 4.60 times for FY2025; Adjusted EBITDA over cash interest paid is 5.43 times LTM (19,216 over an approximated 3,536) and 5.10 times for FY2025. Operating income plus depreciation, depletion and amortization, which excludes equity earnings and the issuer's adjustments, gives total debt over that measure of 3.90 times LTM against 4.65 times for FY2025 (C11); this is a GAAP-based cross-check rather than an issuer measure.
### Claims outside debt
| Item | Amount | Inside or outside the debt figure | Source |
| Operating lease liabilities (current 218 plus non-current 1,644) | 1,862 at September 30, 2026; 1,760 at December 31, 2025 | Outside | Q3 10-Q page:4; 10-K page:286 |
| Sunoco LP lease-related obligations | Included in Sunoco LP's 13,131 line | Inside the debt table | Q3 10-Q page:87 |
| Preferred unitholders' equity | 2,480 (3,356 at December 31, 2025) after the Series H redemption of 900 | Outside | Q3 10-Q page:4 and page:7 |
| Redeemable noncontrolling interests | 266 (250) | Outside | Q3 10-Q page:4 |

Factoring, supply chain finance and a consent decree or equivalent funding obligation were searched for in the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q and no such arrangement was found; the NuStar receivables financing agreement is the only receivables facility, and it had no borrowings. Purchase commitments other than crude oil were not quantified in the pages read and are Not supplied.
### Latest quarter and events to the cutoff

- Q3 2026: Adjusted EBITDA 5,031 against 3,838; distributable cash flow attributable to partners, as adjusted, 2,522 against 1,895 (Q3 release page:8); growth capital expenditures of 1.30 billion US$ and maintenance of 284 million US$ stated in the release (page:2). Guidance for full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was raised to "between $19.7 billion and $19.9 billion" from "$18.8 billion and $19.1 billion" (Q3 release page:2).

- July 2026: junior subordinated notes of 650 and 1,100 issued; 3.90% notes of 550 redeemed (Q3 10-Q page:17). August 17, 2026: Series H preferred units of 900 redeemed (Q3 10-Q page:21; Q3 release page:4); a 14 loss on redemption of preferred units was recorded in Q3 (page:5).
- September 2026: USAC issued 600 of 6.750% senior notes due 2035 (Q3 10-Q page:17).

- October 6, 2026: definitive agreement for Vaquero (above). October 8, 2026: Sunoco LP receivables financing agreement terminated. October 27, 2026: Sunoco LP completed the Offen Parent acquisition for about 600 in cash, "plus working capital adjustments" (Q3 10-Q page:58). October 2026: quarterly distribution of 0.3425 US$ per common unit announced (Q3 10-Q page:58).
- Legal and regulatory matters are described in Note 10 of the Q3 10-Q (Q3 10-Q page:27 onward); their amounts are not summarised here beyond the contingent accrual above.

6. The 9M 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of 11,802 is the sum of the Q1 release (4,098) and Q2 release (3,866 derived as 7,964 less 4,098) and the Q3 release (3,838); it equals the printed nine-month figure (C1). No conflict found.

C1. Adjusted EBITDA reconciliations. Nine months 2026: 6,320 + 4,757 + 2,825 + 516 + 2 + 137 + 519 - 445 + 7 + 588 - 330 + 138 = 15,034, equal to the printed total (Q3 release page:7). Quarters 2026: 4,937 (Q1 release page:7) + 5,066 (Q2 release page:7) + 5,031 = 15,034. Quarters 2025: Q1 4,098 + Q2 (7,964 - 4,098 = 3,866) + Q3 3,838 = 11,802 (Q1 release page:7; Q2 release page:7; Q3 release page:7). FY2025 reconciliation: 5,708 + 5,682 + 3,474 + 350 + 285 + 148 - 130 + 156 + 34 + 726 - 419 - 30 = 15,984 (10-K page:187).

C4. Principal subtotal at September 30, 2026: 51,470 + 565 + 75 + 850 + 13,131 + 2,350 + 111 + 684 + 15 = 69,251. Total debt: 69,251 + 12 - 413 = 68,850, as printed. Parent notes and debentures plus facility: 51,470 + 565 = 52,035. Sunoco LP and USAC: 13,131 + 111 + 2,350 + 684 = 16,276. Change in total debt: 68,850 - 68,333 = 517. Current plus long-term at September 30, 2026: 12 + 68,838 = 68,850; at December 31, 2025: 25 + 68,308 = 68,333.

Parent availability less principal due by September 30, 2027: 4,406 - 4,350 = 56.
C9. Covenant headroom on the stated limit: 5.00 - 2.83 = 2.17 turns. Gap to the simple ratio: 4.28 - 3.21 = 1.07; 3.58 - 2.83 = 0.75. The covenant ratio is as reported; it is not recomputed.
C13. Operating lease liabilities: 218 + 1,644 = 1,862 (September 30, 2026); 245 + 1,515 = 1,760 (December 31, 2025). Total liquidity share at the parent at September 30, 2026: 4,406 of 7,766 undrawn.

spans.text: # CP-1A business and transaction context: Energy Transfer LP (et)
## Request

Module CP-1A for Energy Transfer LP (issuer id et, ticker ET), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, information cutoff 2026-11-05. Current period Q3 2026; prior period FY2025; reporting currency USD. Question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor of the Energy Transfer parent, and how do they reach leverage, liquidity, refinancing and creditor control? Required decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change.

This handoff consumes CP-0 (source readiness, READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS) and CP-1 (financial base). Carried forward from CP-0 and CP-1: the 10-K and 10-Qs control statement facts and the releases are issuer non-GAAP; consolidated debt combines the parent with Sunoco LP and USAC, which have separate facilities; the issuer changed state of organisation and exchange in 2026 and only cover pages and one cross-reference show it; executed debt documents and the partnership agreement are not supplied. Figures from CP-1 are used only as references and are labelled "CP-1". No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is made.
## Sources

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| A diversified US midstream partnership with eight segments, controlled through its general partner by one individual, is growing by acquisition, including a pending 2.63 billion US$ deal, while its state and exchange changed in 2026. | Medium | The partnership agreement, credit documents and the filing recording the 2026 change are not supplied, so control rights and creditor protections rest on summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| No customer exceeded 10 percent of revenue and the largest segment was 24.3 percent of Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA; the Sunoco LP segment supplied the largest part of growth. | Broad asset diversity supports earnings durability, while a large part of earnings growth sits in a subsidiary with its own creditors. | Medium |

| One individual owns 81.2 percent of the general partner and all Class A units, about 20 percent of votes, and unitholders cannot elect the general partner. | Creditors rely on contract terms, not governance rights, to protect their position. | Medium |

| Acquisitions continued: Parkland in 2025, J-W Power, TanQuid, Delta and Offen in 2026, and Vaquero pending with 1.95 billion US$ of cash. | Cash acquisitions add to borrowing needs at the parent and at Sunoco LP and USAC. | Medium |

| In 2026 the parent redeemed 900 US$m of Series H preferred units, funded in part by 1,750 US$m of junior subordinated notes issued in July. | Perpetual preferred equity was replaced by debt-ranking claims below senior notes, raising debt-type obligations. | Medium |

| The cover pages show a change from Delaware to Texas and from the New York Stock Exchange to the Texas Stock Exchange during 2026. | Whether obligors or indenture parties changed is unresolved and must be confirmed before structural work. | Low |
### Business and transaction view

Energy Transfer LP is a large, diversified midstream operator whose eight reportable segments cover natural gas gathering, processing and transportation, NGL and refined products, crude oil, and two publicly traded consolidated subsidiaries: Sunoco LP (fuel distribution and terminals) and USAC (compression). The 10-K states that no customer individually accounted for more than 10 percent of revenue in FY2025, and in Q3 2026 no segment contributed more than a quarter of Adjusted EBITDA on the figures in CP-1, so concentration risk by customer or segment is limited on the documents read. The creditor-relevant features are three. First, change: Sunoco LP acquired Parkland on October 31, 2025, which enlarged that segment's revenue and earnings (it supplied 560 US$m of the 1,193 US$m increase in Q3 Adjusted EBITDA in CP-1) and added subsidiary debt, so the reported leverage improvement depends on a subsidiary with separate creditors. Second, a continuing programme of acquisitions and growth capital: J-W Power, TanQuid, Delta and Offen in 2026, Vaquero agreed on October 6, 2026 for about 2.63 billion US$ (1.95 billion US$ cash plus about 33.3 million new common units), growth capital guided at 5.4 billion to 5.6 billion US$ for 2026 and about 7 billion US$ for 2027. Third, structure and control: the parent's senior notes are unguaranteed by subsidiaries, a single individual controls the general partner, and the issuer's state of organisation and exchange changed in 2026 without a supplied explanation.

What is documented is stated as such below; management language (for example "exceptional product and geographic diversity") is quoted and not adopted. Nothing here is an opinion on creditworthiness. The sponsor field in the context is blank, which is not evidence that no controlling holder exists: the 10-K identifies one.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Source locator | Mechanic and credit implication |

| Core activities | "The primary activities in which we are engaged, which are located in the United States, are as follows: •natural gas operations, including the following: ◦natural gas midstream and intrastate transportation and storage; ◦interstate natural gas transportation and storage; and •crude oil, NGL and refined products transportation, terminalling services and acquisition and marketing activities" | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:6 | Multi-commodity network; earnings depend on volumes, capacity reservation and marketing margins rather than one product |

| Intrastate gas | Approximately 12,200 miles of intrastate pipelines with approximately 24 Bcf/d of capacity; customers pay "a demand fee, which is a fixed fee for the reservation of an agreed amount of capacity" plus transportation fees and fuel retention | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:7 and page:8 | Demand fees give contracted revenue visibility; volume-based fees and gas sales add exposure to throughput and spreads |

| Interstate gas | Approximately 20,090 miles of interstate pipelines with approximately 20.1 Bcf/d of capacity, plus about 7,080 miles through joint ventures; rates regulated by the FERC | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:8 and page:39 | Regulated cost-of-service and negotiated rates stabilise cash flow but face rate-case risk; Panhandle's rate proceedings are on appeal (Q3 10-Q page:60) |

| Lake Charles LNG | Import and regasification terminal with all revenue from "long-term contracts with a wholly owned subsidiary of Royal Dutch Shell plc"; liquefaction development suspended in December 2025 and several offtake agreements terminated | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:9 | Regasification income depends on one counterparty; suspension avoids a large capital commitment, a point for capital discipline |

| Midstream | Gathering, treating and processing with aggregate processing capacity of approximately 13.5 Bcf/d; results "derived primarily from margins we earn from natural gas volumes that are gathered, transported, purchased and sold" | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:10 | Margin exposure to volumes and NGL and gas prices; producer drilling activity is a driver |

| NGL and refined products | About 5,750 miles of NGL pipelines, Mont Belvieu fractionation of 1.15 MMBbls/d, working NGL storage of about 63 MMBbls; revenue "principally generated from fees charged to customers under dedicated contracts or take-or-pay contracts" | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:10 and page:11 | Fee-based contracts with minimum commitments support cash conversion; the segment was the largest contributor to Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA (Calculations C2) |

| Crude oil | More than 18,000 miles of crude trunk and gathering pipelines, equity stakes in seven pipeline systems and about 73 MMBbls of terminal storage; tariffs filed with the FERC and state regulators, plus acquisition and marketing | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:12 | Tariff income is stable; marketing margin is commodity-spread dependent; Bakken Pipeline carries separate project debt |

| Fuel distribution | Sunoco LP distributes "over 15 billion gallons annually to approximately 11,000 Sunoco and partner branded locations"; acquired Parkland on October 31, 2025 with operations in 26 countries | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13 | High-revenue, thin-margin distribution; revenue and margin are exposed to fuel prices, foreign exchange (Canadian dollar functional currency for Parkland) and refinery risk |

| Compression | USAC provides compression services in unconventional plays, "primarily in connection with infrastructure applications" | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13 | Contracted fee income linked to gathering activity; separate credit facility and notes |

| Revenue mix | Gathering, transportation and other fees were 14.5 percent of FY2025 total revenues and 10.0 percent for nine months 2026 (Calculations C1); the rest is product sales including refined products, crude, NGL and natural gas | Analyst Interpretation | 10-K page:287; Q3 10-Q page:4 | Revenue is mostly pass-through product sales, so revenue growth overstates earnings growth; margin analysis must use Adjusted EBITDA (CP-1) |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Pending and recent transactions, with status. Vaquero: on October 6, 2026 Energy Transfer entered a definitive agreement to acquire all equity interests of Vaquero and related assets "for total consideration of approximately $2.63 billion", consisting of $1.95 billion in cash and approximately 33.3 million newly issued Energy Transfer common units; it owns natural gas gathering, processing and transportation assets in the Delaware Basin and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 subject to closing conditions and regulatory approvals (Q3 10-Q page:9 and page:57). The release describes it as a "bolt-on transaction for approximately $2.6 billion" (Q3 release page:2). The source of the cash is not stated, so the effect on the parent's liquidity and debt is Not supplied. For scale only, the cash is 44.3 percent of the parent revolver availability of 4,406 US$m at September 30, 2026 in CP-1 (C5); no funding plan is implied.

Subsidiary transactions: Sunoco LP completed the Offen acquisition for approximately 600 US$m in cash on October 27, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:58), which is a subsequent event after the September 30 balance sheet; Sunoco LP also completed TanQuid on January 16, 2026 for 206 million euros (239 US$m) with assumed debt of 346 US$m fair value, and Delta on April 1, 2026 for about 81 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:57). USAC completed J-W Power on January 12, 2026 for about 912 US$m, of which about 455 US$m was cash and about 457 US$m was 18.2 million new USAC common units (Q3 10-Q page:58). TanQuid was funded using Sunoco LP cash on hand and its credit facility (Q3 10-Q page:57); these subsidiary transactions consolidate into Energy Transfer's debt.

New debt issues and redemptions in 2025 and 2026, from the 10-K and Q3 10-Q. Energy Transfer parent: March 2025, 650 US$m of 5.20% senior notes due 2030, 1.25 billion US$ of 5.70% notes due 2035 and 1.10 billion US$ of 6.20% notes due 2055, with proceeds to refinance debt; August 2025, 1.20 billion US$ of Series 2025A and 800 US$m of Series 2025B junior subordinated notes due 2056; January 2026, 1.00 billion US$ each of 4.55% notes due 2031, 5.35% notes due 2036 and 6.30% notes due 2056; July 2026, 650 US$m of Series 2026A and 1.10 billion US$ of Series 2026B junior subordinated notes due 2057 (together 1,750 US$m), initially at 6.550% and 6.700%, with proceeds to redeem the Series H preferred units, repay Five-Year Credit Facility borrowings and for general partnership purposes (10-K page:325; Q3 10-Q page:17). Redemptions: 4.05% notes of 1.00 billion US$ (March 2025), 2.90% notes of 1.00 billion US$ (May 2025), 5.95% notes of 400 US$m (September 2025), 4.75% notes of 1.00 billion US$ (January 2026), 5.625% notes of 600 US$m (February 2026) and 3.90% notes of 550 US$m (July 2026). Sunoco LP: March 2025, 1.00 billion US$ of 6.25% notes due 2033; September 2025, 1.00 billion US$ of 5.625% notes due 2031 and 900 US$m of 5.875% notes due 2034 to fund Parkland; March 2026, 600 US$m each of 5.375% notes due 2031 and 5.625% notes due 2034, used partly to redeem 500 US$m and 600 US$m of 6.000% notes; Parkland note exchanges in November 2025. USAC: September 2025, 750 US$m of 6.250% notes due 2033; September 2026, 600 US$m of 6.750% notes due 2035.

Preferred and hybrid: the Series H preferred units of 900 US$m were redeemed on August 17, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:19 and page:21); the Series F redemption of 500 US$m occurred in 2025 (10-K page:289; Q3 10-Q page:87). The creditor mechanics are in the CP-1 handoff: the parent's junior subordinated notes are 5,550 US$m in principal on CP-1's calculation, and the preferred equity outstanding fell to 2,480 US$m.

Status labels: Vaquero is agreed and unclosed; Offen is completed after quarter end; the October 8, 2026 termination of Sunoco LP's NuStar receivables financing agreement is completed (Q3 10-Q page:18); the change of state and exchange is documented only on cover pages. Timeline, ownership and conflicts follow.
### Ownership, governance and capital allocation

Control. "Mr. Warren owns an 81.2% membership interest in our general partner and controls our general partner" and "owns all of the outstanding Energy Transfer Class A Units, which represents an approximately 20% voting interest in the Partnership"; the general partner "has the right to appoint and replace the members of the board, including all of its independent directors"; common unitholders "have no right to elect our general partner or the board of directors" (10-K page:132). The filing requires a vote of at least 66 2/3 percent of outstanding common units to remove the general partner and notes that the Class A units vote with the common units, so his holdings make removal harder (Analyst Interpretation). The 851,420,597 Class A units at December 31, 2025 are 19.8 percent of Class A plus common units outstanding (C6), which agrees with the filing's approximate 20 percent. His direct common unit holding is Not supplied in the pages read; the proxy statement is not in the pack. Ownership percentages are not inferred beyond what is stated.

Governance disputes. Unitholders have filed derivative actions against past and current officers, directors, LE GP, LLC and the Partnership as nominal defendant, alleging breach of fiduciary duties related primarily to pipeline construction in Pennsylvania and Ohio, and seeking damages and changes to governance (Q3 10-Q page:32). They are pending and unquantified.

Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility are kept apart. Legal capacity: the senior notes carry covenants including "a limitation on liens, a limitation on transactions with affiliates, a restriction on sale-leaseback transactions and limitations on mergers and sales of all or substantially all of the Partnership’s assets" and are unguaranteed (10-K page:325); the Five-Year Credit Facility has a maximum leverage ratio of 5.00 to 1.00, generally 5.50 to 1.00 in a Specified Acquisition Period (10-K page:330). The documents read do not show financial maintenance covenants on the notes; executed indentures are not supplied. Willingness (documented actions): the Partnership distributes all available cash quarterly and raised the distribution for 2026 quarters from 0.3350 to 0.3425 US$ per unit (Q3 10-Q page:19); it made no unit repurchases in the nine months to September 30, 2026, with 880 US$m remaining under the 2015 programme (Q3 10-Q page:19); it redeemed preferred units with proceeds of junior subordinated notes; it suspended the Lake Charles LNG liquefaction project in December 2025 (10-K page:9). Feasibility: liquidity, leverage and refinancing capacity are in CP-1 (liquidity 8,692 US$m including subsidiary facilities, with 4,406 US$m at the parent).

Behaviour category (issuer level, documented actions only): Neutral or Mixed. Distributions are paid from available cash and increased while growth capital is large, and growing distributions coexist with a falling reported covenant leverage ratio (CP-1) and debt-funded growth. No priming, uptier, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release was found in the pages read. Evidence quality: High for the filings; the scoring dimensions informed are control concentration, distribution policy and capital allocation.

Capital allocation mechanics. Cash acquisitions at the parent and at Sunoco LP and USAC are funded by cash, commercial paper and facility borrowings or new notes, raising consolidated debt unless offset by EBITDA; unit consideration reduces cash needs but increases distributions. Paying 100 percent of available cash leaves growth to be financed by debt and subsidiary-level capital, as CP-1 shows a negative LTM free cash flow after distributions of 873 US$m. Preferred redemption funded by junior subordinated notes raises debt-ranking claims while lowering the preferred coupon base (the notes' initial rates are 6.550% and 6.700%, against 6.500% on Series H, 10-K page:336); this is an Analyst Interpretation.

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: no customer above 10 percent of revenue (10-K page:39); demand-fee and take-or-pay contracts (10-K page:8 and page:11). Mechanic: contracted fee streams cover a share of margin, while marketing, processing margins and fuel distribution vary with commodity spreads. Implication: earnings are more stable than the product-sales revenue suggests, but the proportion of margin that is contracted is Not supplied, so the coverage of fixed charges by contracted income cannot be stated. Counter-evidence: working capital and unrealized commodity swings in cash flow (CP-1).

2. Subsidiary leverage and structural subordination. Evidence: separate Sunoco LP and USAC facilities and notes, and parent notes unguaranteed (10-K page:325; Q3 10-Q page:18). Mechanic: subsidiary creditors rank ahead of the parent in subsidiary assets and cash, while Sunoco LP supplied 560 US$m of the Q3 Adjusted EBITDA increase (CP-1). Implication: the parent's creditors benefit from growth in those subsidiaries only through distributions, so parent leverage measured on consolidated EBITDA overstates parent-available coverage; this is a consideration for CP-2, not a conclusion.

3. Acquisition-led growth and funding. Evidence: Vaquero, Offen, J-W Power, TanQuid and Parkland (Q3 10-Q page:57 and page:58; 10-K page:313). Mechanic: cash components add to borrowings or draw on facilities; unit components dilute distributions per unit. Implication: leverage tolerance depends on EBITDA growth outpacing debt; the Vaquero funding plan is Not supplied, so pro forma leverage is Not calculable.

4. Control and governance. Evidence: 81.2 percent of the general partner and all Class A units (10-K page:132); derivative litigation (Q3 10-Q page:32). Mechanic: unitholders cannot remove the general partner without the vote described, and creditors have no governance rights. Implication: monitoring posture should rest on covenants and disclosure; the partnership agreement is Not supplied.

5. Identity and listing change. Evidence: cover pages and 8-K12B reference. Mechanic: a change of state of organisation could alter the obligor, the governing documents or successor language. Implication: structural analysis should wait for the filing; the conflict logged below counters any assumption of continuity.
6. Key uncertainties: breakdown of contracted versus commodity-linked margin, Vaquero funding, covenant definitions, hybrid treatment, litigation outcomes (Dakota Access and others), and the 8-K12B.
### Conflicts and anomalies (logged, not reconciled)

1. State of organisation and exchange. The 10-K states "Energy Transfer LP is a Delaware limited partnership with common units publicly traded on the NYSE" (10-K page:6) and its cover shows Delaware (10-K page:1). The second-quarter report cover shows Texas with the New York Stock Exchange (Q2 10-Q page:1) and the third-quarter report cover shows Texas with the "Texas Stock Exchange" (Q3 10-Q page:1). The first-quarter report shows Delaware (Q1 10-Q page:1). The Q3 10-Q refers to a "Current Report on Form 8-K12B filed with the SEC on July 6, 2026" (Q3 10-Q page:57), which is not supplied. The effect on the legal entity, indentures and credit agreements is unresolved; the explanation lies outside the sources. Downstream effect: CP-2 cannot assume the 10-K entity is the Q3 obligor.

2. Listing label of subsidiaries. The 10-K says SunocoCorp's units "began trading on the New York Stock Exchange effective November 6, 2025" (10-K page:313) while the Q3 10-Q glossary lists "SunocoCorp LLC (TXSE: SUNC)" and "Sunoco LP (TXSE: SUN)" (Q3 10-Q page:3). Consistent with an exchange move; the dates and reasons are Not supplied.

3. Vaquero value. The 10-Q gives "approximately $2.63 billion" and the release gives "approximately $2.6 billion" (Q3 release page:2); a rounding difference, not a conflict. The cash and unit split is only in the 10-Q.
4. Segment concentration claim. Management says "no single business segment contributing more than one-third"; the calculation gives a maximum of 24.3 percent, so the claim is consistent (C2).
5. Correction to earlier handoffs: none found. CP-1's debt and liquidity figures were reused as references and are not restated here.
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | Readiness | What to take from CP-1A | Why it matters | Gap | Required action |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Structure points: unguaranteed parent notes, separate subsidiary borrowers, control by the general partner, 2026 hybrid issuance and preferred redemption, pending Vaquero, the identity change | Debt priority, recovery mechanics and covenant work depend on which entity owes what | Indentures, credit agreements, partnership agreement, 8-K12B and Vaquero funding are not supplied | Obtain them; build an instrument-level schedule; keep parent and subsidiary claims separate |

| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | The category tags and locators for each fact; management claims are labelled and not adopted | Traceability of the claims in the report | No original HTML or XBRL; chunk locators are not printed page numbers | Verify quotes against the filings; carry the logged conflict |
## Calculations

C1. Revenue mix. FY2025 gathering, transportation and other fees 12,423 over total revenues 85,536 = 14.52 percent (10-K page:287). Nine months 2026: 9,935 over 99,208 = 10.01 percent (Q3 10-Q page:4).

C2. Segment shares of Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 5,031 (Q3 release page:11): NGL and refined products 1,224 = 24.33 percent; Sunoco LP 1,049 = 20.85; crude oil 871 = 17.31; midstream 864 = 17.17; interstate 500 = 9.94; intrastate 346 = 6.88; USAC 198 = 3.94; all other (21) = -0.42. The shares sum to 100 percent (1,224 + 1,049 + 871 + 864 + 500 + 346 + 198 - 21 = 5,031). Sunoco LP share of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA: 2,889 over 15,034 = 19.22 percent.

C3. Cost structure, FY2025: cost of products sold 63,495 over 85,536 = 74.23 percent; operating expenses 5,867 over 85,536 = 6.86 percent; selling, general and administrative 1,180 over 85,536 = 1.38 percent.

C4. Vaquero consideration: 1.95 billion US$ cash plus units; total 2.63 billion US$ less cash 1.95 billion = 0.68 billion US$ of unit value for about 33.3 million units, an implied 20.42 US$ per unit (680 over 33.3). This is an implied figure from the agreement terms, not a market price.
C5. Cash consideration against parent availability: 1,950 over 4,406 (CP-1, September 30, 2026) = 44.26 percent. A scale reference only.
C6. Class A voting share: 851,420,597 over (3,439,986,779 common units + 851,420,597 Class A units) = 19.84 percent (10-K page:132 and page:287). The Class A units vote together with common units.

| Sponsor and prior ownership history: no sponsor; recapitalisation history not found | Low | CP-2 | None |
## Next module
Proceed to CP-2 with CP-0, CP-1 and this handoff. Carry forward:

- The structure: parent senior notes unguaranteed, separate Sunoco LP and USAC credit facilities, hybrid junior subordinated notes and preferred equity as distinct claims, and the control by the general partner owner.
- The unresolved identity point (state and exchange change, 8-K12B), so CP-2 should not assume the 10-K obligor equals the Q3 obligor.

- Subsequent events with dates: Vaquero (October 6, 2026, unclosed, 1.95 billion US$ cash), receivables facility termination (October 8), CPS Energy judgment recorded (October), Offen completed (October 27), project announcements and guidance (November 3 and November announcements).
- Management claims are quoted and labelled, not adopted. Peer ranking, instrument recommendation and recovery conclusions are out of scope.

## Request

It draws on the three upstream handoffs (source readiness, financial base, business and transaction context) and re-checks a few filing pages where a conclusion needed them.
